data.narrative:
Ouster operates in Chips & Semiconductors as a public company. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public peers in the same sector and stage: Cerebras ($39.2B), Credo Semiconductor ($35.8B), and Aeva Technologies ($1.1B). An additional 8 private frontier-tech companies in semiconductors provide secondary reference points, though public comparables are prioritized for established trading signals.

The peer-median method is the primary applicable triangulation approach, anchoring the analysis to the median valuation of same-sector, same-stage peers at $35.8B. This method captures the $1.1B–$39.2B range observed across the three public comps. A public-comp anchoring approach using price-to-sales multiples (21.4x median across ALAB, NVDA, AMD) is not applicable here, as Ouster's revenue figures are not on file and revenue-based valuation is therefore not calculable.

The triangulated valuation range is $30.4B (low) to $41.2B (high), with a median of $35.8B. This range reflects the dispersion in peer valuations and modest sensitivity analysis around the peer median. The primary uncertainty is that only one quantitative method is currently applicable, limiting triangulation breadth. The wide gap between Aeva ($1.1B) and Cerebras ($39.2B) also signals material variance in how the market prices semiconductor hardware companies, depending on technology differentiation and commercialization trajectory. Ouster's current valuation of $2.26B sits materially below the peer median, suggesting either significant discount factors or fundamental differences in comparable companies' cash generation or market positioning that are not captured in peer selection alone.
